verdict_note: From reading only: no build and no tests were run. The core fix holds. The R60-a3 j2 defect is closed: with a path, nothing is written before the bound JobPort is asked. The order as built is: prototype_closed (run, prototype.rs:148), parameter_conflict (:76), path and overwrite parsing, export_path (:89), overwrite_required (:91), one admission (:95 with a document open, else :98-99 on the derived resource), then render, PNG encode and write_atomic (:111-123), then settle_export_job once (:106). An admission refusal (overloaded, canceled or stale_revision) returns before render_and_write runs, so it leaves no file and no temp. After admission, every result reaches settle_export_job: success settles completed, and render, encode, write or prototype_closed failures settle failed with their code. A panic in between drops the AdmittedJob, and Drop settles it Abandoned once (session jobs.rs:552). So each admitted job settles exactly once and its ticket is released once. The derived resource is stable and collision-safe. A play session opened through a command always has a source digest (decode_document passes Some(container), interop-fig-base nodes.rs:2366), so job_resource_invalid cannot be reached from commands. V4-06 holds: no other prototype or play path writes a file. One medium defect should be fixed before the bundled run, because the lane notes misstate it. F1: the no-overwrite check happens before admission and the full render, then write_atomic replaces whatever is at the path. The base checked after the render, so the window covered the PNG encode only. The lane widened it, and the fix is the sibling's one-line write_new. F2-F4 are low and are test gaps and not_proven reasoning; each has a cheap test in the owned paths.

findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/commands/prototype.rs:91 (path.exists() && !overwrite, before admission) and :123 (write_atomic always, which renames over anything present); base: write_png checked exists() after play.render(), so the window was encode_png only; sibling crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/doc_export.rs:936 (export_document: overwrite ? write_atomic : write_new); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/export.rs:202-245 (write_new: symlink_metadata check, then hard_link or exclusive create, refused as destination_exists)
findings.what: overwrite_required is the only no-overwrite guard, and it runs before admission. Between it and the write come the port call, the full frame render (frame PDF export and raster, up to MAX_SCREEN_PIXELS) and the encode. write_atomic then renames the temp over whatever is at the path. A file created there in that window, or a dangling symlink (exists() is false; write_atomic replaces the link), is silently replaced on a capture without overwrite. The lane notes record this TOCTOU as 'unchanged from base', and the lead accepted it as not_proven on that basis. But the lane moved the check from after the render to before admission and the render, so the window grew. The module already has write_new, which closes it, and the sibling export_document uses it whenever overwrite is false.
findings.scenario: Bind a port whose admit() writes b'kept' to the target path, then returns a ticket. This stands in for a concurrent writer inside the window. prototype.capture_frame {path} (no overwrite): the cheap check passes (no file yet), the port creates the file, the render runs, write_atomic replaces 'kept' with the PNG, and the job settles completed.
findings.fix: In render_and_write, pass overwrite through and write with `if overwrite { write_atomic } else { write_new }`, as doc_export.rs:936 does. Map write_new's destination_exists to overwrite_required, so a caller sees one code for 'a file is there'. Keep the early exists() check as the cheap refusal before admission. The late refusal settles the job failed once through settle_export_job.

Capture without overwrite: refused overwrite_required (or destination_exists), the file still holds the known bytes, asks 1, counts (admitted 1, failed 1, released 1, in_flight 0), no *.export-tmp left in the scratch folder.

answers.write_before_admission: None found. Before admission, capture_frame only parses fields, calls Path::file_name and Path::exists, and reads the play session. The render (whose only side effect is the in-memory smart_cache), the encode and write_atomic all run inside render_and_write, which is called only after `admitted.map_err(refused)?` (prototype.rs:100-104). next_correlation() advances an in-memory correlation counter only.
answers.settle_exactly_once: Holds by reading on every path. Ok goes to job.complete (completed, or completed_stale; the head cannot move in this synchronous route). Err covers render (frame_export_refused or frame_render_refused, with the inner code in the detail), encode (the encoder's code), write (export_write or export_path) and prototype_closed (unreachable after the run-level check), and settles Failed(code). The canceled arm is unreachable for this route (F4b). A panic drops the AdmittedJob and settles it Abandoned once (jobs.rs:552-557). An admission refusal holds no ticket. Untested except on the success path (F2).
answers.refusal_leaves_nothing: An admission refusal: no render, no file, no temp. Cheap refusals: nothing. A post-admission write failure: write_atomic removes its temp on write or rename failure (export.rs:185-194). Encode and render failures never create a temp. One gap: a no-overwrite capture can replace a file that appeared after the check (F1).
answers.derived_resource: Stable: SHA-256 over 'hsk.studio.prototype.fig\0' plus FigDocument.source_sha256, the digest of the exact .fig bytes (interop-fig-base import.rs:200). The result is the same in every viewer and process for the same bytes. Collision-safe: 122 hash bits in the UUIDv7 shape (version nibble 7, variant 8-b), and the domain separator differs from audio_import's 'hsk.studio.audio.file\0' and web_site's 'hsk.studio.web.site\0', so equal keys cannot meet across resource kinds. It is keyed by content where the siblings key by path. Edited bytes give a new resource, and two paths holding identical bytes share one. This fits 'derived from the .fig digest' as ruled. It is the third copy of the same 12-line UUIDv7-from-hash snippet (audio_import.rs:879-891, harness-core web_site.rs:1291-1307). A shared helper would sit outside the owned paths; noted only.
answers.tests_vs_implementation: The ask counts are asserted exactly (1 saturated; 1 then 2 open; 0 then 1 for the cheap checks; 0 pathless). Admission before the first byte is proven by behaviour: a saturated port means no file. That the cheap checks come before admission is proven by asks 0 on a saturated port, plus overwrite_required rather than overloaded. Render after admission is not observable (the render has no external side effect) and is not asserted. Weak spots: settlement only on success (F2), and the resource derivation is indistinguishable from a constant (F3). The port of the R60 probe is faithful and stronger (the probe asserted only !(written && asks == 0)).

answers.bounded_work: The pathless capture is bounded by MAX_SCREEN_PIXELS, and the lead accepted it as unadmitted. The admitted cost is {jobs: 1, bytes: 0} (shared admit_export_job_with, the same as export_document). So a capture of up to 16 Mi pixels holds the RGB frame twice (render output plus Samples::U8(screen.rgb.clone()), prototype.rs:113), plus the PNG, outside the port's byte budget. The clone existed at the base. Noted, not a finding: compute screen_json first and move the buffer, if wanted.
